beats.editing_note: Let the course breathe. Show the route map, then cut to terrain-specific B-roll. This is the SETUP phase — grounding the viewer before the data analysis. Pacing: 25-40 sec cuts.

beats.label: THE SCORES — Top 8
beats.narration: The numbers. All fourteen of them. Adventure. 4 out of 5. The kind of ride you'll tell stories about. Remote Vancouver Island forest roads and coastal scenery give the event real destination character. Race Quality. 4 out of 5. The kind of race that spoils you for others. The 2025 operation included a race bible, timed results, 3 routes, packet pickup, food, and awards. Experience. 4 out of 5. The kind of race that reshapes your season. The Vancouver Island setting and 3-distance event provide a memorable regional day beyond a barebones gravel start. Logistics. 3 out of 5. Adequate. The word was invented for this. Nanaimo has airport and ferry access, but Vancouver Island travel still takes more planning than a mainland local race. Length. 3 out of 5. Proper race distance. Enough to hurt. Technicality. 3 out of 5. The course bites if you stop paying attention. Climate. 3 out of 5. Variable. Bring layers and a flexible attitude. Vancouver Island rain, cool starts, and changing forest traction are meaningful preparation constraints. Community. 3 out of 5. Genuine community feel. People stick around. The 2024 results list 107 riders and the BC Gravel Series has a local base, but the event's run was short.
beats.editing_note: PROGRESSIVE RHYTHM: start tight (15-20 sec per dimension), slow down for the most interesting scores (30-40 sec). Each score: number appears, brief pause, explanation. Avatar reacts to extreme scores (5/5 = chef_kiss, 1/5 = facepalm). RE-ENGAGEMENT at 3:00 mark: insert a surprising score reveal or a meme reaction to break the pattern.
